doc: Minimal evidence record for one finding. The five axes are SEPARATE: a defect proven by reproduction stands with incidence unknown; UNKNOWN is not 0; absent telemetry lowers exposure claims, never mechanism truth; a documented exception never turns a failed invariant into PASS; unknown attacker control lowers exploitability confidence, not the observed behaviour. Keep observations and assumptions apart — a reader must be able to tell what was WATCHED from what was inferred.

mechanism_status.doc: What the code/artefact was seen to do. Confirmed needs evidence (file:line, a command and its output, a reproduction).

reproduction.doc: A local reproduction is proof BEFORE any incident — it licenses the finding on its own.

exposure.doc: Who or what can reach the mechanism, or 'unknown'. This is the axis absent telemetry actually lowers.

observed_incidence.doc: 'unknown' | 'never-observed' | a count with its window. UNKNOWN is a word, never a zero.

impact_uncertainty.doc: What is NOT known about the blast, stated — so a rare catastrophic path is not priced as a common trivial one.

observed_scope.doc: What was actually looked at: 'local checkout', a deployment name, a log window.

observed_at.doc: ISO-8601 UTC time of the observation.

observations.doc: What was watched happening, each with its receipt.

assumptions.doc: What was inferred, each named as such — never mixed into observations.

rules: a proven defect may have observed_incidence 'unknown' and remains a finding
an operator interview is asked only when the unknown would change the action
a documented exception changes the decision axis, never the validity axis
